Compute budget versus actual per cost centre and mark overruns
Investigate flagged lines in invoice and hours detail

Write a short memo with options and their cost effect

Workpapers built in personal chatbots cannot be rebuilt for the auditor.

13-2031.00:3405.short: Work out what a new initiative will cost, such as an extra shift, a new client or peak-season flex staffing.

Agree scope, volumes and start date with the requesting manager
Build the cost model from drivers: FTE, CAO rates, shift allowances, flex hours
Sanity-check the result against history and similar past initiatives
Write the resource summary for the requester and the controller

loop.input: checked cost model figures and assumption list
loop.output: one-page resource summary in plain Dutch or English
loop.check: Every number in the text is matched by code to a cell in the model; any mismatch blocks the draft
loop.stop: Two redrafts at most, then fall back to a fixed template with the table only
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template cannot explain which assumptions drive the cost; a short model-written paragraph can, and the number check keeps it honest

13-2031.00:3405.design: A scheduled Python job on a governed data store pulls AFAS GetConnector data (GL, cost centres, headcount) and the agency hours and invoices into one cost base. An Excel or Power BI template then applies defined drivers (CAO rates, shift allowances, agency rates) to the scope the analyst enters. 13-2031.00:3405.still_hard: Agreeing the drivers and keeping the CAO and agency rate tables current. Agency portals may only offer file exports, not APIs. The volume assumptions come from managers and stay uncertain.
13-2031.00:3405.human_edge: Judging whether a manager's volume and timing assumptions are realistic, and knowing which past initiative is a fair comparison.

ambition.what: Cost every client tender and shift change before it is agreed, not only the large ones

13-2031.00:3397.previous_blocker: The hierarchy and the contingency reserve lived in Excel tabs that only the analysts understood. Transfers were typed into AFAS by hand.

13-2031.00:3397.still_hard: Keeping the hierarchy right when cost centres are added or merged. Deciding who may draw on the contingency reserve. AFAS write access needs tight control and an audit trail.
13-2031.00:3397.human_edge: Deciding whether an overrun should come from contingency or be absorbed by the site, and explaining that choice to the controller.

13-2031.00:3400.short: Look for ways to cut cost or raise margin, such as agency overbilling, overtime, idle hours or unprofitable customers.

steps.what: Pull data and scan cost centres and customers for unusual cost or margin
Dig into candidates with site and operations managers
Size the saving or margin gain
Write the proposal and track whether savings are realised

loop.output: one-page proposal with options and owners
loop.check: figures matched to the estimate by script; the analyst edits and approves
loop.stop: one draft; failed figure check returns it to the analyst

13-2031.00:3400.design: Replace the ad-hoc Excel digging with scheduled rule checks on the governed data platform: agency invoices versus approved hours and agreed rates, overtime and idle hours per site, cost per pallet and margin per customer. Results appear as a ranked opportunity list in Power BI with a weekly Teams notice; agreed savings are tracked against AFAS actuals on the same dashboard.
13-2031.00:3400.previous_blocker: Agency, hours and ledger data sat in separate systems joined by hand, so scanning happened only when someone had time or a hunch.
13-2031.00:3400.enabler_now: AI coding makes the joins and rule checks quick to build and maintain; the nightly AFAS extract already feeds Power BI.
13-2031.00:3400.still_hard: Knowing whether an outlier is waste or a reason, such as a peak client order; getting site managers to act; defining cost per pallet consistently across sites.
13-2031.00:3400.human_edge: Hearing from the floor why a cost is high and persuading a site manager to change practice.

13-2031.00:3400.altitude: The analyst stops hunting in spreadsheets and spends the time with site managers on the top five items; they gain the right to put opportunities on the monthly management agenda.
